clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old African American female with type 1 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed at age 10, HgbA1c 7.8%) and documented autoimmune predisposition (anti-GAD and IA-2 positive, IgA deficiency <6.7 mg/dL, HLA DQ2 heterozygous) presented with a 2-month history of nocturnal non-bloody diarrhea, left lower quadrant pain, and nausea. Neurological examination revealed diminished vibration and pinprick sensation in bilateral toes consistent with diabetic neuropathy. She was referred to pediatric gastroenterology and underwent upper and lower endoscopy, which were grossly unremarkable. However, gastric biopsies revealed a histological pattern consistent with autoimmune gastritis. Small bowel biopsies excluded celiac disease. Subsequent serum evaluation demonstrated elevated fasting gastrin level and elevated parietal cell antibodies, without macrocytic anemia or vitamin B12 depletion. The patient was initiated on B12 supplementation (1000 mcg intramuscularly weekly for 8 weeks), which resulted in resolution of her lower extremity symptoms, improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms, and maintenance of normal vitamin B12 levels and complete blood counts.
